title: QBism Logic
abstract: QBism interprets quantum theory as a normative discipline for an agent's probability assignments and their revision across possible experience. This paper develops a logical formalization of that picture. A well-formed core datum consists of an admissible prior space, a finite family of actual measurements, Born kernels, and update kernels. For each such datum, we introduce a guarded dynamic language for histories and posterior states and prove a global reduction theorem. We next consider effectively semialgebraic data over an effectively presented real closed field. For data in this class, we translate the fragment without dynamic operators into first-order formulas in the corresponding language of ordered rings, thereby reducing validity to first-order reasoning over real closed fields. Together, the reduction and first-order translation yield a sound and complete recursive calculus and a decision procedure for validity. Finally, assuming a symmetric informationally complete (SIC) reference measurement, we show that quantum theory in finite dimensions realizes the framework through SIC coordinates, POVMs, and quantum instruments. We also prove that the corresponding SIC image satisfies the standard qplex geometry conditions, namely the consistency bounds and the lower polar condition, and that under explicit coefficient field hypotheses the resulting quantum datum is effectively semialgebraic.
summary: This paper constructs a logical framework (QBism Logic) to formalize how agents update their beliefs based on quantum measurements. It achieves this by showing that the structure governing these updates can be translated into first-order logic over real closed fields, yielding a decidable calculus. Crucially, it demonstrates that standard finite-dimensional quantum mechanics fits perfectly within this abstract mathematical structure.
main_problem: The paper develops a rigorous logical formalization of QBism (Quantum Bayesianism), interpreting quantum theory as a normative framework for an agent's probability assignments and their revision based on experience.
main_result: It establishes that the structure describing quantum updates, when restricted to effectively semialgebraic data over real closed fields, yields a sound, complete, and decidable recursive calculus. Furthermore, it shows standard finite-dimensional QM fits this framework using SIC coordinates.
method: The methodology involves developing a guarded dynamic language for histories, translating the logic fragment into first-order formulas in ordered rings, and applying algebraic geometry tools (qplex conditions) to verify quantum realizations.
model_or_system: The model is QBism Logic applied to finite-dimensional quantum systems. The core structure is defined by a 'well-formed core datum' $(Q, \mathcal{D}, B, U)$, involving admissible prior spaces, measurement families ($\mathcal{D}$), Born kernels ($B$), and update kernels ($U$).

important_parameters: The dimension parameter $d \ge 2$, and the underlying structure is assumed to be effectively semialgebraic over a real closed field $K$.
main_assumptions: Assumes the existence of an SIC reference measurement in finite dimensions, and relies on explicit coefficient field hypotheses for the effective semialgebraic reduction theorem.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the general logical structure (Chunk 2), then proving a global reduction theorem to eliminate dynamic operators (Chunk 1/4), followed by translating this into first-order logic over real closed fields for decidability (Chunk 1/4), and finally demonstrating that standard quantum mechanics realizes this framework under SIC assumptions, confirming its semialgebraic nature (Chunk 3).
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical foundation connecting operational quantum theory to formal logic and model theory. For theorists working on open quantum systems or measurement processes, it offers a rigorous, decidable calculus for reasoning about state updates.
